lessons.title: Preflight enforcement-layer existence before locking around it
lessons.pattern: A LOCK handoff cited M15 signed-commit atomicity as the enforcement layer for a two-write split. Three Thesis Team passes + tightening pass emerged READY_TO_LOCK at the design-coherence layer. None checked whether the cited enforcement existed on-disk. Pre-execution preflight surfaced the gap: workspace not under git, no .git/ on disk, M15 is documentation not infrastructure. Red Team v2 actually flagged 'two-write procedure is operator-discipline, not system-enforced' (v2 A-3); the response was to relabel the missing infrastructure CLOSURE-REQUIRED. Taxonomy is not enforcement.
lessons.pre_check: Before any LOCK handoff is dispatched and before any Thesis Team round is scoped to bless one, the handoff author runs an enforcement-layer existence audit. For every mechanism the design names as load-bearing (signed commits, pre-commit hooks, CI gates, OS primitives, external services, runtime modules), tag each as EXISTS (with on-disk evidence), ASPIRATIONAL (not yet built; design must NOT depend on it for correctness), or OUT-OF-SCOPE (different system, not a dependency). Any load-bearing ASPIRATIONAL mechanism blocks the LOCK until either (a) redesign around an EXISTS-tier mechanism, or (b) scope to the future phase that brings the ASPIRATIONAL mechanism online. Audit is the first artefact of the LOCK handoff (00_enforcement_layer_existence_audit.md); inspected before Thesis Team dispatch. Architectural corollary: prefer designs whose enforcement lives inside the system being designed, over designs whose enforcement lives in external infrastructure the operator may or may not have set up. Sovereignty Promise applies recursively.

lessons.title: GPP bootstrap: one-time exception for mechanism-gating-its-own-commit
lessons.pattern: When introducing a mechanism whose purpose is to gate commits of plan-layer artifacts, the commit that defines the mechanism cannot itself be gated by that mechanism without a circular dependency. The mechanism does not exist on disk yet; the commit IS the mechanism coming online. Two naive paths both fail: (a) refuse to LOCK anything until GPP is already LOCKed — infinite regress; (b) LOCK the mechanism with zero audit discipline — defeats the purpose. The third path is the bootstrap exception: build the tool, run it on itself + its paired commits, amend-run-repeat until clean at the tool level, then use the operator + synthesis-tier model synthesis tier to dispose residual findings, then LOCK the mechanism commit explicitly labeled as bootstrap. Subsequent commits never bootstrap — they are GPP-gated from their first dispatch, because GPP now exists on disk.
lessons.pre_check: Before any LOCK of a new plan-layer-gating mechanism, the author verifies: (a) the mechanism's tool runs and emits a report on itself + all paired commits (even FAIL must be disposed in bootstrap synthesis); (b) the bootstrap commit is labeled in front-matter as 'amendment_status: DRAFT — bootstrap exception — L-007 applies'; (c) a daily-log entry documents the bootstrap one-time exception with pointer to Thesis-round transcript, findings list, disposition rationale per finding; (d) subsequent plan-layer commits never reference L-007 as justification for skipping GPP — one-time exception class, not ongoing escape hatch; (e) the mechanism's spec file contains a 'boot-strap path' section explicitly naming itself as the boot-strap case.

lessons.title: OpenClaw config set bracket-quote path pollution: use Python-patch for allowlist writes
lessons.pattern: OpenClaw's documented syntax for setting a quoted-key allowlist entry — `openclaw config set 'agents.defaults.models["groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile"]' '{}' --strict-json` — inserts TWO keys into the allowlist: the intended clean `groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile` AND a polluted `"groq/llama-3.3-70b-versatile"` with literal quote characters embedded in the key name. Same bug affects `openclaw config set --batch-file <file>` when the batch JSON uses the documented `["quoted.key.path"]` syntax. The polluted keys are functionally dead (they match no model) but clutter the config and could confuse future parsers or drift-detection logic.
lessons.pre_check: Never write to `agents.defaults.models` via `openclaw config set`. Use a Python patch that reads ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, edits the allowlist dict directly, and writes back. After any Python patch, run `openclaw config validate --json` to confirm schema integrity. Back up `openclaw.json` to a dated `.safety-bak-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ` before every patch. OpenClaw's own .bak rotation keeps only last 4-5 rotations, so operator-controlled backups are separate insurance.
lessons.related: openclaw models aliases add works correctly and does NOT hit this bug (different config path / code path). Aliases ARE safe to edit via CLI. Known CLI pitfall: even with clean allowlist, --model <alias> resolves to anthropic/<alias> instead of aliased model. Aliases work as documentation only; all real invocations must use full provider/model-id form.
lessons.origin: Agent SDK Thesis cross-family audit attempt 2026-04-19. First via batch-file, then via individual config set calls per Plan agent's recommendation. Both polluted. Workaround Python-patch succeeded and became canonical.

lessons.title: Anthropic batch custom_id regex forbids colons; use underscores
lessons.pattern: Anthropic's /v1/messages/batches validates each custom_id against ^[a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}$. The natural namespacing pattern <orgSlug>:<workflow>:<uuid> uses a colon as separator, which the API rejects with a 400 invalid_request_error. The colon-separator pattern is what most humans reach for first (and is what pipeline/handoffs/caching_batch_build_handoff_2026-04-19.md §D1 specified before the constraint was known).
lessons.pre_check: any code generating custom_id for Anthropic batches must (a) use `_` or `-` as separator, (b) strip or replace characters outside [A-Za-z0-9_-], (c) cap total length at 64. Strip UUID dashes to keep length budget: <slug>_<workflow>_<uuid_no_dashes> fits 64 chars for typical slugs (~10) + workflow (~15) + 32-char uuid.
lessons.mitigation_applied: tilth/bin/tilth-batch.mjs customId() uses underscore separator, strips invalid chars from slug/workflow, strips UUID dashes, length-caps to 64. Live-verified on msgbatch_01KcJAvWrovZoHyxrcBvmEc6 (2-request smoke batch, both rows succeeded).

lessons.title: Transport-retry carve-out: retry on transport artifacts, count as cycle-1
lessons.pattern: Committee reviewers occasionally return transport-layer artifacts — reasoning-tag spills, gateway placeholders ('Agent couldn't generate a response'), hallucinated findings referencing non-existent modules while the top-line verdict is PASS, mid-round provider model deprecations. Treating these as cycle-1 substantive disagreement forces premature E3 operator synthesis on rounds that were clean at the substance layer; treating every failed payload as retriable without discipline opens an escape hatch around the L-005 two-audit ceiling.
lessons.pre_check: Carve-out fires ONLY when: (a) payload is unparseable as expected JSON verdict OR parseable-but-internally-inconsistent (e.g., PASS verdict with findings referencing modules not in the review packet) OR gateway-side error placeholder; AND (b) prompt is unchanged between attempts (substantive-invariant); AND (c) retry is logged explicitly in amendment/synthesis.md as '<seat> <transport-artifact-kind> retry; substantive-invariant'. Retries under this carve-out DO NOT count against the L-005 retry cap of 1. Retries that change the prompt OR surface new substantive content DO count and are NOT transport retries.
lessons.origin: Logician v2.2 Wave 1 (F-AMDT-02 llama reasoning-tag spill). Committee API credits are real; half-closed queues are worse than deferred ones.'

lessons.title: Faithfulness-consolidation Thesis round: new round class, narrower than semantic review
lessons.pattern: When a consolidation artifact rolls up N individually-LOCKED inputs (e.g., a §N v2.X consolidated amendment rolling up 12 per-gate LOCKs already validated), the appropriate Thesis round is NOT a full semantic re-review of the component semantics — those already passed their own per-component rounds. A full semantic re-review burns reviewer tokens re-litigating decisions already LOCKED; a zero-review merge has no integrity floor. The faithfulness-consolidation round splits the difference: 5-reviewer single dispatch against 6 criteria (faithfulness-to-inputs / no-additions / cross-refs-resolve / ordering-preserved / front-matter-coherent / companion-code-pins-verifiable). Zero semantic findings is the expected outcome; any semantic finding is a regression signal pointing back to a per-component round that did not hold.
lessons.pre_check: Before dispatching a Thesis round on a consolidation artifact, classify the round type explicitly in the spec card's round_type field: semantic_review (first-time LOCK) / verification_reaudit (L-005 v2) / faithfulness_consolidation (roll-up of N already-LOCKED inputs, NEW per this lesson) / retroactive_confirmation (L-013 supplementary round under different roster). If faithfulness_consolidation, the review prompt restricts reviewers to the 6-criteria scope and explicitly excludes semantic re-review. Reviewers who surface semantic findings get re-prompted with scope restriction (not a transport retry; a scope-reframe retry). Per-component LOCK evidence paths must be listed in the spec card for reviewer access.
lessons.applies_to: §N v2.X consolidated blueprint amendments; lock_history.v1.jsonl backfill batches; MEMORY.md consolidation passes; any artifact whose content is derivable from union-of-LOCKED-inputs.

lessons.title: BLUEPRINT_DEPS pin narrow-fix MUST verify section numbers against blueprint TOC, not just the pin hash
lessons.pattern: The TestBlueprintDepsPin family pinned by the Batch 2/3 narrow-fix asserts only deps[blueprint_file]['hash_sha3_512_prefix16'] == 'dafb038260486f64' and deps[blueprint_file]['version'] == 'v7.1'. This means the pin hash catches *blueprint-file drift* (blueprint changes → hash changes → pin fails) but does NOT catch *code-claim drift* (code author mistypes §2.9 when they mean §2.7 — pin hash is still correct because the blueprint file is unchanged). The Batch 3 committee surfaced both mis-anchors as HIGH findings against the blueprint-adherence criterion, blocking promotion. lessons.title: Supersession-discipline must propagate through handoff prompts
lessons.pattern: When a persona prompt is superseded (banner added to old file, new canonical file authored), the supersession lives ONLY at the prompt-file layer. Handoff prompts that load the persona by path are NOT auto-rewired — they continue to point at the old path until manually updated. Result: a handoff dispatched the same day a supersession lands can run the OLD persona despite the supersession banner being on disk. The Session B handoff went further — it editorialized the staleness as deliberate ('v1 is still current; v2 superseded scope only, not identity'), entrenching the drift. The new public-field ports v2.1 added (anti-rationalization table, must-find-at-least-one rule, severity auto-promotion, self-review trap breakers, nightly mode) were silently absent from Wave 3 + Wave 4 review surfaces. The 5/5 PASS cycle-1 outcome on F-AMDT-05 (Wave 3) and subsequent Wave 4 closures looked clean — but ran the OLD reviewer discipline, not the upgraded one.
lessons.pre_check: When authoring or LANDING a persona supersession, the same commit (or a paired commit landing same-day) MUST: (1) add SUPERSEDED banner to old persona file (already standard); (2) `grep -lr <old_persona_path> pipeline/handoffs/ pipeline/engineering/ orgs/` and update EVERY hit to new path — do NOT exempt 'already dispatched' handoffs; (3) for genuinely closed handoffs, append one-line drift-correction note rather than deleting; (4) add one-line PRE-check note to the active handoff: 'Verify: grep king_midas_implementation_prompt_v pipeline/handoffs/<latest>.md resolves to current version. If it points to a SUPERSEDED file, STOP and ping operator.'; (5) file daily-log entry naming every handoff updated, every handoff that ran under the stale path before correction, and any review surfaces (committee dispatches, gate LOCKs) that landed under stale persona — those LOCKs are NOT invalidated, but a 'ran-under-stale-persona' footnote is appended to relevant lock_history rows OR captured in memory entry for traceability.

lessons.title: Red Team probe set must include whimsical / OOD attacks, not just rubric-aligned ones
lessons.pattern: Standard adversarial-review prompt libraries are organized around the rubric the draft will be scored against. This is rubric-aligned probing, and it is necessary. But MS Research 2026-05 demonstrated that 'whimsical' adversarial strategies — surreal framing, role inversion, ambiguous instruction, time-pressure, format-spoof — expose failure modes that standard safety tests miss because the modes live out-of-distribution from how reviewers normally attack. The probe-library deficiency is structural: a Red Team prompt set built only from the rubric will never probe what the rubric does not name. Cross-family rigor between Scribe / Judge / Red Team mitigates family-of-prior bias but does not mitigate family-of-attack bias.

Scribe and Judge clear those probes alongside rubric-criterion adversarial pressure. Five families are seed taxonomy, not closed set — Red Team operators expand as new OOD failure modes are observed.

lessons.title: No-supersession-for-comments principle: YAML comment-only edits to LOCKed cards do NOT require new lock_history rows, §0.5 paired-commits, or re-signing
lessons.pattern: Canonical-JSON / SHA3-512 / Ed25519 signature computation for a LOCKed card runs yaml.safe_load BEFORE any hashing step. YAML comments are not represented in yaml.safe_load's output dict — they are stripped at parse time. Therefore the SHA3-512 hash and Ed25519 signature pinned in the lock_history row are computed over the comment-free canonical bytes; any edit that touches ONLY YAML comments (lines beginning with `#`, including comment-block borders and pre-block documentation paragraphs) cannot change those canonical bytes, regardless of how many comments are added, removed, or reworded. The pinned hash stays identical post-edit; the pinned signature still verifies against the publisher pubkey. Consequently, comments-only refinements to LOCKed cards do NOT require: (a) a new lock_history.v1.jsonl row, (b) a §0.5 paired-commit ceremony, (c) re-signing under the publisher key, or (d) a supersession banner. The complement boundary line is that ANY edit that lands inside the canonical body (a value in admin_risk_term_register, a new top-level field, a sub-field inside _research_metadata, prose values in _review_handback, or any non-comment YAML at all) DOES change canonical bytes, DOES break the pinned signature, and DOES require the full supersession path (§18 narrow-corrective supersession + new lock_history row + re-sign).
lessons.pre_check: Before applying a documentation-only refinement to a LOCKed card under pipeline/cards/, the author confirms: (1) Scope is strictly comments-only — every edited line is a comment line, a comment-block border line, or whitespace adjustment between comment lines; no value, key, sub-field, or non-comment YAML line is touched. (2) Canonical-bytes verification fires post-edit — run the ceremony-script canonical-bytes computation (yaml.safe_load → set _research_metadata.ed25519_signature to None → json.dumps(sort_keys=True, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=False) → hashlib.sha3_512) against the post-edit card and compare to the pinned SHA3-512 and to Ed25519-verify against the pinned publisher pubkey. Pre/post equality on hash AND signature-verify is the gate. Any mismatch means the edit slipped outside comments-only — STOP, revert, surface to operator for supersession path decision. (3) No lock_history row appended — per Done-definition (handoff documentation-only convention), no row is required and none should be added. Single audit-trail row at operator discretion only. (4) No §0.5 paired-commit — §0.5 paired-commits are for canonical-body changes paired with their architecture / blueprint / lessons co-changes; comments-only refinements have no canonical-body delta. (5) Completion handoff cites this lesson — the completion handoff for a comments-only round names L-023 explicitly as the controlling principle and includes the pre/post hash + sig-verify evidence inline (OD-I 2026-05-16 handoff at pipeline/handoffs/od_i_completion_2026-05-16.md is the canonical-shape precedent).
lessons.boundary_clarification: This lesson is narrowly about YAML files whose canonical-bytes computation strips comments via yaml.safe_load (the cards under pipeline/cards/*/*.yaml, governed by the ceremony script pipeline/scripts/cards_wave_2_lock_ceremony_2026-05-16.py). It does NOT generalize to artifacts whose canonical-bytes computation preserves comments (e.g., JSON files, markdown blueprints whose entire textual body is canonical, Python modules whose comments and docstrings are part of source-of-truth). For those classes, comment edits DO change canonical bytes and DO require the full supersession path. Authors must verify their target artifact's canonical-bytes computation strips comments before invoking L-023.

lessons.title: Don't conflate grant logic with credit underwriting logic; stacked funding stacks separate mechanisms
lessons.pattern: Grant logic and credit underwriting logic are objectively different financial-access mechanisms even though they serve adjacent client needs. The real-world use case is stacking different funding types — e.g. USDA VAPG grant + low-interest farm loan + PA tourism grant + PA small business loan + PA small business advantage grant — each with its own matching logic, eligibility rubric, scoring axes, and underwriting (or non-underwriting) mechanics. Conflating them into Track A / Track B of a single CLC is a category error: Track A and Track B partition by partition_axis WITHIN a single financial-access mechanism (e.g., personal-guarantee vs cooperative-membership inside credit_underwriting), not ACROSS distinct mechanisms. Each instrument deserves its own CLC at runtime. The failure surfaced at OD-E when the Cowork session was about to compose grant-rubric content (KGIE / funder-tradition / probe-coverage discipline) into credit_underwriting's Track B partition — operator HALT triggered the L-005 substance-gap discipline, and path (a) acceptance preserved the structural amendment (§18.6 v2 dual-track schema-shape extension landing top-level track_a:/track_b: containers per OD-C value-position regex) without forcing a fabrication.
lessons.pre_check: Before authoring Track B (or Track N) content onto a multi-track CLC card, the author confirms: (1) Both tracks share the same financial-access mechanism — credit underwriting, grant evaluation, equity placement, debt service, working-capital line, in-kind sponsorship — distinct mechanisms ALWAYS get distinct CLCs. (2) partition_axis names a within-domain split (e.g., personal-guarantee vs cooperative-membership inside credit_underwriting), NOT a cross-mechanism split (credit-readiness on one side vs grant-readiness on the other). (3) Stacking use case spawns separate CLCs, not adjacent tracks — when one client pursues multiple instruments (grant + loan + tourism grant + small business advantage grant), each instrument's matching logic is authored on its own CLC; the stacked outcome is composed at runtime across CLCs, not folded into a single CLC's track pairs. (4) Structural amendments without authored substance default to path (a) acceptance — where a schema-shape amendment lands top-level track_a:/track_b: containers without authored substantive Track B content, preserve the structural amendment, defer Track B substance to its proper-domain CLC; any attempt to fabricate cross-domain content onto an adjacent CLC's Track B is a category error and MUST be halted at the L-005 substance-gap. (5) HALT triggers a domain-clarification record at three surfaces: the affected card's _partition_provenance.domain_clarification block, the structural amendment file's 'Domain rationale' appendix, and the ceremony's CEREMONY_SUMMARY.md operator-decision section.
lessons.boundary_clarification: This lesson is narrowly about CLC cards whose partition_axis field would imply a track-pair within a single financial-access mechanism. It does NOT apply to: (a) CIC cards (client-instrument-context partition, not multi-track); (b) RFA cards (single funder + single mechanism by definition); (c) single-track CLC cards whose schema does not land top-level track_a:/track_b: containers. For those classes the partition-axis convention is established by their own card-class precedent and L-024 does not bind.

lessons.title: Pre-ceremony, amendment files should be authored with amendment_status: LOCKED <ceremony_timestamp_utc> from the start, not flipped post-ceremony
lessons.pattern: If an amendment file is authored with amendment_status: DRAFT and then flipped to amendment_status: LOCKED <ceremony_timestamp_utc> AFTER the ceremony script computes canonical-JSON / SHA3-512 / Ed25519, the on-disk canonical bytes change post-sign. The pinned hash in the lock_history row no longer matches the post-flip on-disk bytes; the pinned Ed25519 signature no longer verifies against re-computed canonical bytes from the post-flip file. The only recovery is a supersession row that re-pins SHA3-512 + Ed25519 against the LOCKED-state canonical bytes, with the historical pre-flip row preserved verbatim in audit trail per the row-170 transparent-disposition pattern. This mirrors the OD-D row 269 supersession-of-row-241 byte-restoration pattern (§18 main file re-pinned post-Phase-4 fold-in checklist append; row 241 canonical bytes superseded by row 269). At OD-E, row 274 pinned the §18.6 v2 amendment file at DRAFT-status canonical bytes; row 279 was required as recovery supersession to register the LOCKED-status canonical bytes once the operator flipped the amendment_status field. The supersession row is a permanent audit-trail entry that could have been avoided entirely by authoring amendment_status: LOCKED <ceremony_timestamp_utc> from the start, matching the timestamp the ceremony script will use.
lessons.pre_check: Before any paired-commit LOCK ceremony fires against an amendment file, the ceremony author confirms: (1) amendment_status: is LOCKED <ceremony_timestamp_utc> BEFORE canonical-bytes computation — not DRAFT, not READY_TO_LOCK, but LOCKED with the exact ceremony timestamp embedded. (2) Embedded timestamp matches the ceremony's locked_at_utc / timestamp_utc field character-for-character (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ ISO-8601 Z-suffixed UTC). (3) Operator-driven ceremony timing uses the script-substitution pattern — the ceremony script computes datetime.now(timezone.utc) at its entrypoint, substitutes that value into the amendment file's amendment_status: field via in-place edit, and ONLY THEN computes canonical-JSON / SHA3-512 / Ed25519; substitution and hashing happen in the same script run, strictly in that order. (4) Post-ceremony status-flip is a process antipattern — if observed, the operator MUST file a recovery supersession row (mirror of OD-D row 269 / OD-E row 279 pattern: historical pre-flip row preserved verbatim, new row pins LOCKED-state canonical bytes, supersession verdict explicit) AND a daily-log entry naming the L-025 firing. (5) Ceremony-script linter fail-fast (deferred) — the ceremony script template at pipeline/scripts/*_lock_ceremony_*.py should fail-fast on amendment files whose amendment_status: value is DRAFT (or anything other than LOCKED <timestamp>) at canonical-bytes computation time; pre-flight assertion parallel to L-006 enforcement-layer existence audit; deferred to v0.2 ceremony-script hardening if not landable inside v0.1.
lessons.boundary_clarification: This lesson applies to any artifact whose canonical-bytes computation runs over a field that may change between authoring and signing (the amendment_status: front-matter case is the canonical instance, but the principle generalizes to any pre-ceremony-mutable field: lock_status:, verdict:, signed_at:, etc.). It does NOT apply to artifacts whose canonical-bytes computation is invariant under post-author edits in that field (e.g., if the field is stripped before hashing per L-023's yaml.safe_load-strips-comments analog) — but the default discipline assumption is that the field IS part of canonical bytes unless explicitly proven otherwise by the ceremony script's logic.

lessons.title: Never embed heredocs inside $() command substitution; macOS bash 3.2 parser bug fires on parens / backticks in body
lessons.pattern: Bash 3.2 (the macOS default shell version) has a long-standing parser bug around heredocs embedded inside $(...) command substitution. Even when the heredoc delimiter is single-quoted (<<'TAG'), if the body contains shell-meaningful tokens — (, ), backticks, certain quoting patterns — the outer parser scans the body for command-position syntax BEFORE the inner heredoc quoting can neutralize it. This produces errors like "syntax error near unexpected token )" on lines deep inside what should be inert body content. The natural first instinct for operator-runnable bash scripts that need multi-line string content (issue bodies, comment text, prompt envelopes, etc.) is VAR=$(cat <<'EOF' ... EOF). Sandbox bash -n passes (Linux bash 5.x). On macOS — where #!/usr/bin/env bash resolves to /bin/bash 3.2 unless Homebrew bash is in PATH — the parser bug fires at runtime. Failure shape: 'command substitution: line N: syntax error near unexpected token )' where line N points into the heredoc body, typically near literal parens like (rows 234/235) or (or equivalent), or near a backtick inside otherwise-literal prose. The single-quoted delimiter is correct discipline and is necessary, but is not sufficient on bash 3.2 because the outer-context scanner runs before the inner-quoting takes effect for ) / backtick matching.
lessons.pre_check: Before handing any bash script to the operator for execution on macOS, audit for VAR=$(cat <<'TAG' ... TAG) patterns. Refactor each to one of three bash-3.2-safe alternatives: (1) Temp-file pattern (preferred for multi-line bodies) — WORKDIR=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf $WORKDIR' EXIT; cat > $WORKDIR/body.md <<'TAG' ... TAG. Top-level heredoc, no $() wrapping. Consume via the tool's --body-file / -f flag (gh issue create --body-file, gh issue comment --body-file, etc.). Canonical pattern. (2) read -r -d '' with || true — IFS= read -r -d '' VAR << 'TAG' || true; ...; TAG. Works in bash 3.2 because the heredoc is the input to read, not a substituted command. The || true is required because read returns 1 on EOF and would trip set -e. (3) Top-level assignment with line continuation (acceptable for short bodies) — VAR='line 1\nline 2'. No heredoc, no command substitution. Loses syntax-highlighting friendliness for long content but is bulletproof. Verification step: bash -n <script> MUST pass in the sandbox AND the script SHOULD additionally be sanity-checked under the constraint that the operator's bash version may be 3.2. The sandbox-pass-without-thinking-about-3.2 failure mode is the actual lesson here — bash -n passing on Linux bash 5.x does NOT guarantee macOS bash 3.2 will parse the file. Heredoc-inside-$() is the single most common 3.2-vs-5.x divergence pattern; treat any sandbox script containing that pattern as suspect by default.
lessons.boundary_clarification: This lesson applies to bash scripts intended for the operator's local environment (Mac mini, any Cowork-side artifact ending in .sh). It does NOT apply to scripts that run only inside the Cowork sandbox (Linux bash 5.x). The decision rule: if the operator will bash <script> on their own machine, assume bash 3.2 compatibility is required unless the operator has explicitly opted into Homebrew bash by setting #!/usr/bin/env bash AND has bash 4+ first in PATH. The safer default is to write 3.2-compatible scripts regardless.
lessons.sibling_to: L-002 (path references, never content dumps — both are scripting/prompt-hygiene disciplines; L-002 is about minimizing prompt-token cost, L-026 is about minimizing macOS shell-compatibility footguns; both surface most often when an agent writes a script in a Linux sandbox and the operator runs it on Mac); L-013 (validation discipline — bash -n is the script-level equivalent of the Magic Step; passing bash -n in the sandbox is necessary but not sufficient when the runtime shell may differ).

lessons.title: .gitignore globs like **/*secret* match filenames, NOT directories; presumed-private dirs need explicit path-entries
lessons.pattern: .gitignore glob patterns match against path components, not against directory containment. The pattern **/*secret* matches any path component containing the substring 'secret' — so it covers _private/auth_secret_key.txt, vault_shared/funder_secret_notes.md, and pipeline/secret_handoff.md, but does NOT cover vault_shared/key_rotation_policy.md (no 'secret' substring in the filename or any parent directory name). The intuitive assumption 'files under vault_shared/ are private by default' is wrong — vault_shared/ is gitignored only for specific paths explicitly listed (e.g., vault_shared/machine_calibration.json); everything else in vault_shared/ commits publicly. The Track 9 audit comment that established the **/*secret* glob covered the filename-substring case but did NOT establish directory-scope coverage; treating it as the latter is a category error.
lessons.pre_check: Before writing any new file to a directory whose contents are 'presumed private' (vault_shared/, _private/, orgs/, etc.), the author MUST run `git check-ignore -v <new_path>` AFTER the file lands. If it returns exit 1 (not ignored) AND the file should be private, one of the following MUST land in the same commit: (1) Explicit path entry in .gitignore — `vault_shared/key_rotation_policy.md` (canonical for files that semantically belong at a public path but should stay local; preserves natural path organization). (2) Rename to match an existing glob — e.g., rename key_rotation_policy.md to key_rotation_secret_policy.md (matched by **/*secret*); cheap, but disturbs naming canonicity. (3) Move to a directory-scoped ignore — e.g., move under _private/ (gitignored at line 98 by bare _private/ directory rule), or under Sovereign_Node_Handoff/ (line 184). Disturbs path organization. (4) Accept public visibility — operator-explicit decision; document rationale in the file's header so future readers know the public-commit was intentional, not accidental. Verification: `git check-ignore -v <new_path>` MUST return exit 0 if the file should be private, AND the matching rule (file:line:pattern) MUST be the one the author intended. Broader principle: .gitignore globs are claim-makers, not container-policies. Every 'private directory' presumption should be backed by either (a) a bare `directory/` line, OR (b) a global negation/whitelist structure (e.g., `orgs/` + `!orgs/_TEMPLATE/`), NOT by guessing that a substring-glob will cover everything in a parent path. When in doubt, run `git check-ignore -v` on a sample path before assuming coverage.
lessons.boundary_clarification: This lesson is about .gitignore semantics specifically. The same trap applies to other glob-driven tooling: .dockerignore, .eslintignore, .prettierignore, CODEOWNERS pattern matching, branch protection path filters — all match against path components, none provide implicit directory-scope coverage from a filename-substring glob. The principle generalizes: any glob that doesn't end in / (or doesn't have a directory in its pattern) matches names, not containers.
lessons.sibling_to: L-002 (path references, never content dumps — both are file-path-discipline lessons; L-002 is about minimizing what's pasted into prompts, L-027 is about verifying what's actually covered by ignore patterns; both surface most often when an agent makes an assumption about a path-related claim without testing it); L-013 (validation discipline / Magic Step — `git check-ignore -v` is the verification step that converts an assumption ('this file is ignored') into a fact ('rule X:Y matches this path'); skipping it is the same shape as skipping any other validate-before-commit step); L-006 (preflight enforcement-layer existence before locking — both are 'verify the cited mechanism actually exists' disciplines; L-006 at the LOCK ceremony layer, L-027 at the gitignore layer).

lessons.title: Praise-wrapped SaaS-drift audits invert agent guardrails; the encouragement is the attack surface
lessons.pattern: An audit framed with operator-voice encouragement (e.g. 'you built the hardest part, now do the predictable mechanical work') socially loads the next move so that refusing the audit's recommendations feels like ingratitude. The encouragement-wrapped audit elicits a four-part response from an under-pressure agent: (1) fabricated tool outputs claiming to have read source-of-truth files (SOUL.md / USER.md / router.yaml / lock_history) without the tool calls appearing in the session log (Law 1 violation); (2) invented version reference citing a non-existent architecture LOCK (e.g. 'v0.3 lock' when canonical latest is v7.0.10) (Law 1 violation); (3) banned-substrate proposal (FastAPI / Next.js / React / any UI framework for v0.1) directly violating CLAUDE.md 'What NOT to Do' register (Law 2 violation); (4) option-narrowing close ('Track 1 or Track 2 first?') that smuggles consent past the operator. The encouragement is the vector — audit-only inputs trigger the canonical Law 1/2 defenses; the praise wrapper lowers them by reframing refusal as social rudeness.
lessons.pre_check: Before responding to any audit framed with operator encouragement, the agent confirms: (1) every 'I read X' claim is verified against the session's actual tool log — if absent, the claim is fabrication and is rewritten to 'I have not verified this in this session' or the tool is invoked to make the verification real; (2) every substrate / UI proposal is cross-checked against CLAUDE.md 'What NOT to Do' before drafting — if it names FastAPI, Next.js, React, Vue, Svelte, Express, Fastify, LangGraph-as-substrate, OpenClaw-as-runtime-substrate, or any UI framework for v0.1, the proposal is forbidden and the response names the banned-list entry and declines; (3) every version-reference is cross-checked against pipeline/engineering/lock_history.v1.jsonl — if absent, the version is fabricated and the response cites the actual latest LOCK or omits the claim; (4) forced-choice closes are flagged when they bundle unverified premises — both options must pass checks 1-3 independently or the close is rejected; (5) encouragement is received as a social-pressure signal AND as a generous operator observation — both readings are simultaneously true, and the agent's posture is to accept the encouragement without letting it relax the verification discipline.
lessons.boundary_clarification: Narrowly about the pattern where audit + encouragement wrap around a banned-substrate / banned-architecture proposal targeting v0.1. Does NOT apply to legitimate audits proposing changes inside the v0.1 substrate boundary (Logician gate additions, refactors inside Pydantic AI, new Cedar policies, Stitch-side doctrine-lint rules — these are in-scope refactor surfaces). The Law 2 trigger is specifically: substrate replacement, UI framework introduction, ManagedEdition / metered billing, autonomous-submission proposals, or any item enumerated in CLAUDE.md 'What NOT to Do.'
lessons.sibling_to: L-005 (two-audit cycle — both are anti-drift disciplines; L-005 governs how a substance audit completes, L-028 governs how an audit-input is received without inverting the substance gate). L-013 (Magic Step validation discipline — the pre-checks are the same shape: an assertion is not a fact until verified). L-016 (supersession-discipline propagation through handoff prompts — both are propagation disciplines; L-016 governs that downstream prompts inherit supersession context, L-028 governs that an agent receiving an audit prompt inherits the CLAUDE.md 'What NOT to Do' check). L-021 (Red Team OOD / surreal probes — L-021's role-inversion probes are the prospective adversarial test that L-028's pattern is the empirical failure of).
